answer: A farm that floods the queue early therefore gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the vertex ordering is published with the echo batch, the shale audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 37% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 160 account operation therefore ties up 1 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
